newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Schindler sees rising business in C.Europe.
newsitem.headline: Schindler sees rising business in C.Europe.

text.p: Europe's leading elevator manufacturer Schindler Holding Ltd expects to quadruple its annual sales to one billion Austrian schillings in Central Europe by 2000, company officials said on Tuesday.

"I hope that by 2000 the zone (central Europe) where I work will generate an annual turnover of one billion Austrian schillings," Hans-Joachim Baurle, Vice President of Schindler's eastern European operations, told a news conference.
"Currently the 1,000 people working in this region generate a turnover of 250 million schillings," he said.
The Switzerland-based company, whose central European activity is controlled from Austria, plans to increase its presence in Hungary, Czech Republic, Poland and Slovakia.
It also plans to start operating in Russia by the end of this year and is negotiating to cooperate with a Romanian elevator company, Schindler said in a statement.

Schindler Hungaria Kft expects its sales to surpass one billion forints in 1996, and foresees breaking even this year after being in the red last year and seeing some profits by 1997, managing director Janos Munnich said.
"Our sales revenue doubled in the past three years and for this year we expect sales over one billion forints," Munnich said.
Schindler Hungaria's sales amounted to 930 million forints in 1995, accounting for 0.2 percent of the Switzerland-based Schindler Holding Ltd's total revenues.
